title: IB Business Management Past Papers: Final Weeks
summary: IB Business Management past papers become a focused final-weeks system: practise under time, self-mark accurately, log errors, and revisit weak topics.
body_markdown:
The final weeks before an IB Business Management exam are not for collecting more resources. They are for turning what you know into marks under pressure.


Archived exam papers are useful because they expose the distance between recognising a concept and applying it precisely. A student may understand economies of scale, for example, yet lose marks by failing to connect the concept to the organisation in the stimulus. Timed attempts, careful self-marking, an error log, and focused repair work close that gap.


The process is simple:


- Complete a paper or section under realistic time conditions.
- Mark it using the official markscheme and relevant markbands.
- Record why each mark was lost.
- Revisit the weakest topic or skill.
- Answer a fresh question to test whether the weakness has been repaired.


That final step matters. Reviewing an error creates awareness. Answering a new question proves whether anything changed.


### Begin with a realistic final-weeks plan


Doing a full paper every evening may feel ambitious, but volume without reflection produces surprisingly little improvement. A better plan alternates performance and repair.


Session Main task Purpose


Day 1 Timed paper or major section Reveal current weaknesses


Day 2 Self-mark and build an error log Diagnose lost marks


Day 3 Review weak topics and command terms Repair knowledge and technique


Day 4 Complete targeted questions Test the repair


Day 5 Sit another timed section Check whether performance improved


Repeat the cycle rather than moving through papers mechanically. If your evaluation is consistently superficial, another full paper will merely reproduce the same problem over more pages.


Use the[IB Business Management Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-business-management/questionbank) to isolate the topic, command term, or response type causing difficulty. RevisionDojo's guide to[using an IB Question Bank effectively](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-question-bank-or-how-to-use-it-effectively) explains how targeted sets can support this feedback loop.


### Make timed attempts genuinely timed


A timed attempt should imitate the decisions required in the examination. Put away notes, use only permitted equipment, and stop when the allocated time ends. If you continue for another 20 minutes, you are measuring eventual knowledge rather than exam readiness.


The current course, first assessed in 2024, gives SL students two external papers. Paper 1 lasts 1 hour 30 minutes and is worth 30 marks, while Paper 2 lasts 1 hour 30 minutes and is worth 40 marks. HL students also sit the 30-mark Paper 1, a 50-mark Paper 2 lasting 1 hour 45 minutes, and the 25-mark Paper 3 lasting 1 hour 15 minutes.


Those differences should shape your practice. HL students need dedicated Paper 3 preparation rather than treating it as an extension of Paper 2. The[Paper 3 17-marker planning guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/writing-a-business-plan-for-the-ib-business-management-paper-3-17-marker) is useful when your recommendations lack structure or strategic justification.


Before beginning, divide the available minutes sensibly across the marks. Do not let a familiar low-mark calculation consume time needed for an extended response. During early attempts, record when you start and finish each section. This shows whether the problem is slow reading, excessive planning, hesitant calculations, or overwritten conclusions.


A student rewards a calculator for its arithmetic before an examiner asks what the answer means


### Use the IB Business Management markscheme actively


Many students treat the markscheme like a final scorecard. It is more valuable as a map of how credit is awarded.


First, mark in a different colour. For short responses, identify the exact knowledge, application, or calculation step that earned each mark. For extended responses, compare your answer with both the question-specific guidance and the relevant markband. The course uses analytic markschemes alongside markbands for the 10-mark responses in Papers 1 and 2, so spotting a familiar phrase is not enough. The quality of analysis, balance, application, and judgement also matters.


Use three labels while marking:


- **Secure:** the point clearly meets the requirement.
- **Borderline:** the idea is present but vague, unsupported, or weakly applied.
- **Missing:** the answer does not satisfy the requirement.


Be conservative. If you cannot explain why a sentence deserves a mark, do not award it automatically. When uncertain, compare the response with the[IB Business Management 10-marker rubric guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/understanding-the-ib-business-management-10-marker-rubric) or ask a teacher to review the disputed section.


Then rewrite one weak paragraph. This is where the markscheme becomes learning rather than accounting. A better paragraph should use relevant evidence from the case, explain the business consequence, acknowledge a limitation where appropriate, and connect back to the question.


### Build an error log that leads to action


An error log should capture causes, not merely topics. Writing “finance” is too broad to guide tomorrow's revision. Writing “calculated gross profit correctly but interpreted the margin without comparison” gives you something specific to fix.


Create columns for:


- Paper and question
- Topic or tool
- Command term
- Marks available and marks earned
- Reason marks were lost
- Corrective action
- Date retested


Most errors fall into four categories: knowledge, application, technique, and time. A missing definition is a knowledge problem. Generic discussion that ignores the stimulus is an application problem. A one-sided answer to an evaluate question is a technique problem. An unfinished conclusion is often a time problem.


Patterns become visible after two or three sessions. Perhaps calculations are accurate but interpretations are weak. Perhaps recommendations sound sensible but never discuss constraints. The[Business Management marks format guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-business-management-marks-format-explained) can help distinguish what different response types require.


### Revisit weak topics without rereading everything


Once the log identifies a weakness, choose the smallest resource capable of repairing it. Use Study Notes for an unclear concept, Flashcards for definitions and formula recall, or AI Chat to question your understanding. The aim is not to restart the syllabus.


Suppose your break-even calculation is correct but your written interpretation lacks context. Reviewing every finance chapter wastes time. Instead, revise the meaning of the result, inspect a worked response, and complete two questions requiring interpretation. Revision should follow the diagnosis.


Use[exam-style Business Management questions](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-exam-style-questions-practice-with-authentic-formats) to test the repaired skill in unfamiliar contexts. If the same error appears again, refine the intervention. You may need feedback from RevisionDojo's Grading tools or Tutors rather than another round of independent notes.


### Move from targeted practice to Exam mode


Targeted practice builds individual skills. Full simulation teaches you to coordinate them.


In the last 7-10 days, move between short Questionbank sets and complete timed papers. RevisionDojo's[IB Exam Builder guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-exam-builder-custom-practice-paper-guide) explains how to create a custom paper and complete it in timed Exam mode. Predicted Papers and Mock Exams can provide fresh material when familiar questions no longer offer a reliable test.


After every simulation, calculate more than the total. Compare performance by topic, command term, and question length. A stable score hiding repeated weaknesses is less reassuring than it looks.


Do not introduce a complicated new system in the final 48 hours. Review the recurring entries in your error log, rehearse essential formulas and structures, and protect sleep. Coursework Library examples can deepen understanding earlier in the process, but the final days should remain centred on examination decisions.


### Turn each attempt into the next mark


The value of an exam paper is not the number written at the top after marking. Its value is the next decision it changes.


A rushed calculation teaches you to show working. A generic paragraph teaches you to apply each claim to the stimulus. An unbalanced recommendation teaches you to consider constraints before judging. Small corrections accumulate because the same habits appear across many questions.


RevisionDojo brings that cycle together. Practise weak areas in the Questionbank, reinforce knowledge with Study Notes and Flashcards, seek clarification through AI Chat, and use Grading tools to sharpen extended responses. Then sit Predicted Papers or Mock Exams in Exam mode under honest time conditions. In the final weeks, the ultimate IB resource is not the one with the largest pile of material. It is the one that helps you notice, repair, and retest what costs you marks.
